title: Corpus EUR-Lex via Cellar HTTPS
platform: Windows 11, Python 3.12 environment managed by uv

runs.note: First real download from Cellar over HTTPS (8 requests, at most 1 per second), writes data/corpus.lock. Same code as the commit above, run just before it was committed.
Cache emptied, the four texts downloaded again and checked against the committed lock: same sha256, same article counts.

runs.command: sed 's/"articles": 64/"articles": 63/' data/corpus.lock > data/cache/tampered.lock && vigie-ingest --only DORA --lock data/cache/tampered.lock
runs.note: Gate seen red: an article count that differs from the lock stops ingestion.

runs.command: sed 's/"sha256": "b1ae/"sha256": "0000/' data/corpus.lock > data/cache/tampered-sha.lock && vigie-ingest --only DORA --lock data/cache/tampered-sha.lock
runs.note: Gate seen red: a hash that differs from the lock stops ingestion.

runs.command: python -m ruff check . ; python -m ruff format --check . ; python -m mypy src

observations: https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/{CELEX} answers 303 with a Location in plain HTTP; the fetcher follows it by hand, upgrades it to HTTPS and refuses any other host. The HTTPS form of that Location answers 200 with the same bytes.
AMLR annex ids carry a no-break space (anx_ followed by U+00A0 then I): eid is cleaned to anx_I, the EUR-Lex link keeps the published id percent-encoded.
Recitals are excluded by default and indexed with --recitals.
